text: Lets developers build encapsulated components that manage their own state and compose into complex UIs
quote: Build encapsulated components that manage their own state, then compose them to make complex UIs.

text: Can be added to an existing HTML page to render interactive components without a full rewrite
quote: You don’t have to build your whole page in React. Add React to your existing HTML page, and render interactive React components anywhere on it.

text: Uses JSX, a markup syntax extension that lets you write rendering logic together with markup
quote: This markup syntax is called JSX. It is a JavaScript syntax extension popularized by React.

text: Components can be passed new data (e.g. from user input) and React updates the screen to match
quote: You can pass them new data in response to an interaction, like when the user types into an input. React will then update the screen to match the new data.

text: Recommends using a full-stack meta-framework like Next.js or React Router to build a complete app
quote: To build an entire app with React, we recommend a full-stack React framework like Next.js or React Router.

text: React Native and Expo let you build native Android/iOS apps reusing React skills
quote: React Native and Expo let you build apps in React for Android, iOS, and more. They look and feel native because their UIs are truly native.

text: On the server, React can stream HTML progressively while data is still being fetched
quote: On the server, React lets you start streaming HTML while you’re still fetching data, progressively filling in the remaining content before any JavaScript code loads.

text: React can render on the server using Node.js
quote: React can also render on the server using Node and power mobile apps using React Native.

text: You can adopt React incrementally, using as little or as much of it as needed on a page
quote: you can use as little or as much React as you need

text: Frameworks built on React support fetching data in async server components, even at build time
quote: Frameworks that implement it let you fetch data in asynchronous components that run on the server or even during the build.

text: React components are plain JavaScript functions, so you can use standard if/map logic for conditionals and lists
quote: React components are JavaScript functions. Want to show some content conditionally? Use an `if` statement. Displaying a list? Try array `map()`.
